title: Quasi-coherence over a quasi-coherent algebra agrees with quasi-coherence over the structure sheaf
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal A$ a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_S$-algebras whose underlying $\mathcal O_S$-module is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. An *$\mathcal A$-module* is a sheaf of $\mathcal A$-modules on $S$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; it is an $\mathcal O_S$-module through the structure map $\mathcal O_S\to\mathcal A$. An $\mathcal A$-module $\mathcal G$ is *quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal A$-module* if every point of $S$ has an open neighbourhood $W$ with an exact sequence $\bigoplus_{j\in J}\mathcal A|_W\to\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal A|_W\to\mathcal G|_W\to0$ of $\mathcal A|_W$-modules, for some sets $I,J$ (direct sums taken in the category of $\mathcal A|_W$-modules). Then an $\mathcal A$-module $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal A$-module if and only if its underlying $\mathcal O_S$-module is quasi-coherent.

proof.text: *Step 1 (forgetting from $\mathcal A$-modules to $\mathcal O$-modules).* Let $W\subseteq S$ be open, $\mathcal O_W=\mathcal O_S|_W$, $\mathcal A_W=\mathcal A|_W$ with structure map $\sigma:\mathcal O_W\to\mathcal A_W$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] to the site of opens of $W$ (every presheaf of abelian groups on a topological space has a sheafification) and to each of the sheaves of rings $\mathcal O_W$ and $\mathcal A_W$. (a) *Direct sums.* For a family $(\mathcal G_i)_{i\in I}$ of $\mathcal A_W$-modules a direct sum $(\Sigma,(\iota_i))$ in $\Mod(\mathcal A_W)$ exists (clause (2)); its underlying $\mathcal O_W$-module, with the $\iota_i$ (which are $\mathcal A_W$-linear, hence $\mathcal O_W$-linear), is a direct sum of the underlying $\mathcal O_W$-modules in $\Mod(\mathcal O_W)$. Indeed let $(\Sigma',(\iota'_i))$ be a direct sum in $\Mod(\mathcal O_W)$ (clause (2)) and $c:\Sigma'\to\Sigma$ the $\mathcal O_W$-linear map with $c\iota'_i=\iota_i$. By clause (3) for $\mathcal O_W$ and for $\mathcal A_W$, the underlying abelian sheaves of $(\Sigma',(\iota'_i))$ and of $(\Sigma,(\iota_i))$ are both coproducts in $\Ab(W)$ of the underlying abelian sheaves of the $\mathcal G_i$, and $c$ commutes with the coprojections, so $c$ is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves: every $c_V$ is bijective, its inverse is $\mathcal O_W(V)$-linear, and $c$ is an isomorphism in $\Mod(\mathcal O_W)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. (b) *Exactness.* For $\mathcal A_W$-linear maps $\mathcal P\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal Q\xrightarrow{v}\mathcal G$, the sequence $\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q\to\mathcal G\to0$ is exact in $\Mod(\mathcal A_W)$ if and only if the underlying sequence of $\mathcal O_W$-modules is exact in $\Mod(\mathcal O_W)$: exactness means $vu=0$, $\operatorname{Coker}v=0$ and $\ker v=\operatorname{Im}u$ ($\operatorname{Im}u=\ker(\mathcal Q\to\operatorname{Coker}u)$); by clause (1) the forgetful functors of both categories to $\Ab(W)$ preserve kernels and cokernels, hence images, and are faithful, so both conditions are equivalent to the exactness of the underlying sequence of abelian sheaves.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Lemma 03DA (sites-modules-lemma-abelian) and Lemma 03DB (sites-modules-lemma-limits-colimits); used tacitly in Morphisms, Lemma 0H88, proof, first paragraph: 'Then this is also an exact sequence of O_U-modules' (written out by the agent)

proof.text: *Step 2 (direct sums of copies of $\mathcal A$ on affines).* Let $W\subseteq S$ be open, $I$ a set and $(\Sigma,(\iota_i)_{i\in I})$ a direct sum of copies of $\mathcal A_W$ in $\Mod(\mathcal A_W)$; put $e_i=\iota_{i,W'}(1)$ on any open $W'\subseteq W$, so that $\iota_{i,W'}(a)=a\,e_i$ by $\mathcal A_W$-linearity. Let $U\subseteq W$ be an affine open, identified with $\operatorname{Spec}R$, $R=\mathcal O_S(U)$ [def-pc-scheme], and let $A=\mathcal A(U)$, an $R$-module through $\sigma_U:R\to A$; let $c_i:A\to\bigoplus_IA$ be the summand inclusions and $\tau:N\to\Gamma(U,\widetilde N)$ the maps of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction]. *Claim:* there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules $\theta:(\bigoplus_IA)^\sim\to\Sigma|_U$ with $\theta_U(\tau((a_i)_i))=\sum_ia_ie_i$ (finite sum) for $(a_i)\in\bigoplus_IA$; consequently the underlying $\mathcal O_W$-module of $\Sigma$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Proof: $\mathcal A|_U$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2) (open immersion $\operatorname{Spec}R\cong U\subseteq S$), so by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3) the counit $\varepsilon:\widetilde A\to\mathcal A|_U$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules, and $\varepsilon_U\circ\tau=\mathrm{id}_A$ because $\varepsilon$ corresponds to $\mathrm{id}_A$ under the bijection $\alpha\mapsto\alpha_U\circ\tau$ of clause (1). By Step 1(a), $(\Sigma,(\iota_i))$ is a direct sum of copies of $\mathcal A_W$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_W)$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](1) (open immersion $U\subseteq W$) $(\Sigma|_U,(\iota_i|_U))$ is a direct sum of copies of $\mathcal A|_U$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](4), $((\bigoplus_IA)^\sim,(\widetilde{c_i}))$ is a direct sum of copies of $\widetilde A$. Hence there is a unique $\mathcal O_U$-linear $\theta$ with $\theta\circ\widetilde{c_i}=\iota_i|_U\circ\varepsilon$ for all $i$, and it is an isomorphism (a family of isomorphisms between the summands induces an isomorphism of direct sums). On sections over $U$, using $\widetilde{c_i}_U\circ\tau=\tau\circ c_i$ (clause (1)): $\theta_U(\tau(c_i(a)))=\iota_{i,U}(\varepsilon_U(\tau(a)))=\iota_{i,U}(a)=a\,e_i$, and $\tau((a_i))=\sum_i\tau(c_i(a_i))$ gives the formula by additivity. Quasi-coherence: every point of $W$ lies in an affine open $U\subseteq W$ (the affine opens of the scheme $S$ form a basis of its topology [def-pc-scheme]), and $\Sigma|_U\cong(\bigoplus_IA)^\sim$; this is the definition of quasi-coherence [pqf-def-coherent].

proof.text: *Step 3 (quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal A$-module $\Rightarrow$ quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal O_S$-module).* Let $\mathcal G$ be quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal A$-module and $x\in S$. There are an open $W\ni x$, sets $I,J$ and an exact sequence $\Sigma_J\xrightarrow{u}\Sigma_I\xrightarrow{v}\mathcal G|_W\to0$ in $\Mod(\mathcal A_W)$, $\Sigma_I,\Sigma_J$ direct sums of copies of $\mathcal A_W$ there. By Step 1(b) it is exact in $\Mod(\mathcal O_W)$, i.e. $v$ is a cokernel of the $\mathcal O_W$-linear map $u$ in the abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O_W)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so $\mathcal G|_W\cong\operatorname{Coker}u$ as $\mathcal O_W$-modules. By Step 2 the underlying $\mathcal O_W$-modules of $\Sigma_I$ and $\Sigma_J$ are quasi-coherent, so $\operatorname{Coker}u$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image](2) applied on the scheme $W$ (an open subscheme of $S$ [def-pc-scheme]); quasi-coherence is invariant under isomorphism (an isomorphism $\mathcal F|_U\cong\widetilde M$ composes with one $\mathcal G|_U\cong\mathcal F|_U$), so $\mathcal G|_W$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. In particular $x$ has an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq W$ with $\mathcal G|_U=(\mathcal G|_W)|_U\cong\widetilde M$ for a module $M$ over $\mathcal O_S(U)$. As $x$ was arbitrary, the underlying $\mathcal O_S$-module of $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 0H88 (morphisms-lemma-quasi-coherence-scalar-restriction), proof, first paragraph (line 1855 ff.)

proof.text: *Step 4 (converse: the module over an affine and its presentation).* Let $\mathcal G$ be an $\mathcal A$-module whose underlying $\mathcal O_S$-module is quasi-coherent, $x\in S$, and $U\ni x$ an affine open, identified with $\operatorname{Spec}R$, $R=\mathcal O_S(U)$ [def-pc-scheme]. Put $A=\mathcal A(U)$, a commutative $R$-algebra through $\sigma_U$, and $M=\mathcal G(U)$, an $A$-module through the action of $\mathcal A(U)$ on $\mathcal G(U)$; its $R$-module structure as a section module of the $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal G$ is $r\cdot m=\sigma_U(r)m$, i.e. the restriction of scalars along $\sigma_U$ (this is the 'translation of the $\mathcal A$-module structure into an $A$-module structure on $M$' that the source omits). $\mathcal G|_U$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2), so by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3) the counit $\varepsilon_{\mathcal G}:\widetilde M\to\mathcal G|_U$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules, with $(\varepsilon_{\mathcal G})_U\circ\tau=\mathrm{id}_M$ (clause (1), as in Step 2). Presentation of $M$: let $I=M$ as a set, $\alpha:\bigoplus_{m\in I}A\to M$, $(a_m)\mapsto\sum_ma_mm$, which is $A$-linear and surjective; let $J=K=\ker\alpha$ as a set and $\beta:\bigoplus_{k\in J}A\to\bigoplus_IA$, $(a_k)\mapsto\sum_ka_kk$, whose image is $K$. So $\bigoplus_JA\xrightarrow{\beta}\bigoplus_IA\xrightarrow{\alpha}M\to0$ is an exact sequence of $A$-modules, hence of $R$-modules; that is, $\alpha$ is a cokernel of $\beta$ in $R$-modules. For $k\in K$ write $k_m\in A$ for its component at $m\in I$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 0H88, proof, second paragraph ('We have isomorphisms of O_U-modules A|_U = A~ and F|_U = M~ ... (details omitted). Choose an exact sequence ... of A-modules'); details written by the agent

proof.text: *Step 5 (the $\mathcal A|_U$-linear maps).* Let $(\Sigma_I,(\iota_m))$ and $(\Sigma_J,(\iota'_k))$ be direct sums of copies of $\mathcal A|_U$ in $\Mod(\mathcal A|_U)$ (Step 1(a)), with $e_m=\iota_{m}(1)$, $e'_k=\iota'_k(1)$ as in Step 2. For a section $g\in\mathcal G(U)$ the maps $\mathcal A(V)\to\mathcal G(V)$, $a\mapsto a\cdot g|_V$ ($V\subseteq U$ open) form an $\mathcal A|_U$-linear map $\mathcal A|_U\to\mathcal G|_U$, since restriction is compatible with the actions [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; likewise for a section of $\Sigma_I$ over $U$. By the universal property of direct sums let $v:\Sigma_I\to\mathcal G|_U$ be the $\mathcal A|_U$-linear map with $v\iota_m=(a\mapsto a\,m|_V)$ for $m\in I=M$, and $u:\Sigma_J\to\Sigma_I$ the one with $u\iota'_k=(a\mapsto a\,s_k|_V)$, where $s_k=\sum_mk_me_m\in\Sigma_I(U)$ (finite sum). On sections over $U$, by $\mathcal A(U)$-linearity, $v_U(\sum_ma_me_m)=\sum_ma_mm=\alpha((a_m))$ and $u_U(\sum_ka_ke'_k)=\sum_ka_ks_k=\sum_m\bigl(\sum_ka_kk_m\bigr)e_m$, and $\sum_ka_kk_m$ is the $m$-th component of $\beta((a_k))$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 0H88, proof, second paragraph ('this produces an exact sequence ... of A~-modules'); written out by the agent

proof.text: *Step 6 (exactness, and conclusion).* Let $\theta_I:(\bigoplus_IA)^\sim\to\Sigma_I$ and $\theta_J:(\bigoplus_JA)^\sim\to\Sigma_J$ be the isomorphisms of Step 2 (with $W=U$), and $\widetilde\alpha,\widetilde\beta$ the images of the $R$-linear maps $\alpha,\beta$ under the functor $N\mapsto\widetilde N$ of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](1), so $\widetilde\alpha_U\circ\tau=\tau\circ\alpha$, $\widetilde\beta_U\circ\tau=\tau\circ\beta$. Then $v\circ\theta_I=\varepsilon_{\mathcal G}\circ\widetilde\alpha$ and $u\circ\theta_J=\theta_I\circ\widetilde\beta$ as $\mathcal O_U$-linear maps: by the bijection $\gamma\mapsto\gamma_U\circ\tau$ of clause (1) it suffices to compare them after $\tau$ on global sections, and by Steps 2, 4, 5: $v_U(\theta_{I,U}(\tau(a)))=v_U(\sum_ma_me_m)=\alpha(a)=(\varepsilon_{\mathcal G})_U(\tau(\alpha(a)))=(\varepsilon_{\mathcal G})_U(\widetilde\alpha_U(\tau(a)))$ for $a\in\bigoplus_IA$, and $u_U(\theta_{J,U}(\tau(b)))=u_U(\sum_kb_ke'_k)=\theta_{I,U}(\tau(\beta(b)))=\theta_{I,U}(\widetilde\beta_U(\tau(b)))$ for $b\in\bigoplus_JA$. So the sequence of underlying $\mathcal O_U$-modules $\Sigma_J\xrightarrow{u}\Sigma_I\xrightarrow{v}\mathcal G|_U\to0$ is isomorphic, through $\theta_J,\theta_I,\varepsilon_{\mathcal G}$, to $(\bigoplus_JA)^\sim\xrightarrow{\widetilde\beta}(\bigoplus_IA)^\sim\xrightarrow{\widetilde\alpha}\widetilde M\to0$. The latter is exact in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$: $\alpha$ is a cokernel of $\beta$ (Step 4) and $N\mapsto\widetilde N$ preserves colimits [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](4), so $\widetilde\alpha$ is a cokernel of $\widetilde\beta$, which in the abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is exactness of the sequence. Hence the sequence $\Sigma_J\to\Sigma_I\to\mathcal G|_U\to0$ is exact in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$, and by Step 1(b) (with $W=U$) it is exact in $\Mod(\mathcal A|_U)$. Since $x\in U$ was arbitrary, $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal A$-module. With Step 3 this proves the equivalence.
